text:
Marathon Petroleum dropped 1.9% today, continuing a sharp two-week decline of 9.3%. The immediate trigger appears to be a leadership change announced yesterday (Oct 29) combined with caution from analysts ahead of Big Oil earnings reports — CNBC flagged that while earnings may surge, investors should watch guidance closely, suggesting concern about forward profitability. The stock has now fallen steeply three days running, wiping out earlier October gains.

The broader backdrop is mixed for refiners. Oil prices remain elevated ($103 domestically, $123 globally), and U.S. refineries are running at a robust 92.8%, which should support margins. However, escalating Middle East tensions—Iran claiming tanker strikes near the Strait of Hormuz and reported U.S. military reshuffles—create uncertainty about whether geopolitical risk will spike costs or disrupt supply chains. That uncertainty, combined with the leadership transition and analyst caution on guidance, appears to have spooked investors despite still-favorable refining conditions.
